MT4-0587.stem: A state servant holds a position in a federal agency and also works part-time at a technical institute. The agency plans to procure research services. As part of their official duties, the state servant must help draft the technical specification for this work. They know that the technical institute is interested in performing the work under the planned state contract and intends to enter the competition. In this situation:

options.a: There is a conflict of interest because, if the technical institute wins, the state servant's workload there will increase, which may in turn affect the quality and volume of their official work at the federal agency
options.b: There is a conflict of interest because the state servant can influence the technical specification and give an advantage to an organization from which they receive income
options.c: There is no conflict of interest because there is no information indicating that the decision could provide a material benefit to the state servant or their family members
options.d: There is no conflict of interest because, compared with other potential bidders, the technical institute can perform the work to the highest standard and at a reasonable price
options.e: There is no conflict of interest because there is no evidence that the state civil servant intends to abuse their official position

MT4-0588.stem: A state body announced a competition to award subsidies to socially oriented non-profit organizations. The non-profit organization Mercy and Care entered the competition. One state servant involved in evaluating applications and deciding on subsidies had previously worked for this charity, although at the time of the competition they had no financial obligations linking them to it. Believing that Mercy and Care most deserved support, the state servant actively described its advantages and persuaded commission members to vote for it. Under the Federal Law On the State Civil Service of the Russian Federation, in this situation:

options.a: There was no conflict of interest, but official-conduct requirements were breached
options.b: There was no conflict of interest if the charity would have received the subsidy even without the civil servant's support
options.c: There was a conflict of interest because the civil servant used their official position to obtain a material benefit for a particular charity

MT4-0589.stem: A citizen entered the state civil service in 2011. In 2013, the civil servant's wife and her parents jointly purchased an apartment in shared ownership. The wife's expenditure was 2 million rubles; the apartment cost 4 million rubles.

options.a: The civil servant must report the wife's expenditure if the couple's combined income for 2011–2012 is less than 2 million rubles
options.b: The civil servant must report the wife's expenditure if the couple's combined income for 2011–2012 is less than 4 million rubles
options.c: The civil servant must report the wife's expenditure if the couple's combined income for 2010–2012 is less than 2 million rubles
options.d: The civil servant must report the wife's expenditure if the couple's combined income for 2010–2012 is less than 4 million rubles

MT4-0590.stem: In 2005, A. was appointed deputy head of a division in a territorial office of a federal service. In 2009, A.'s husband was appointed head of that territorial office. A review of compliance with official-conduct requirements found no corruption in the interaction between the head and state servant A.: there were no inflated bonuses, privileges, preferences or similar benefits. In this situation:

options.a: There is no conflict of interest because A. was appointed to the territorial office before her husband became its head
options.b: There is a conflict of interest, but because the review found no abuse of powers by the head, both state servants may remain in their positions under continuous monitoring of the conflict by the conflict-of-interest commission
options.c: Because the head can appoint and dismiss staff, approve their duties and perform other personnel-management functions, A. is directly subordinate to her husband; a restriction associated with state civil service has therefore been breached, and one spouse must be dismissed from the territorial office
options.d: There is neither a conflict of interest nor a breach of a state civil service restriction because, although A.'s husband heads the territorial office, he is not her immediate supervisor

MT4-0591.stem: Civil servant K. holds a position in the Federal Service for Environmental Protection. She also teaches part-time at an Institute of Natural Resource Management. Her official work is closely related to the subjects she teaches at the institute. In this situation:

options.a: State civil service legislation is complied with as long as K. does not use, in her teaching, official information learned through performing her civil service duties
options.b: State civil service legislation is complied with if the employer's representative at K.'s place of service knows about her secondary employment and has no objections to it
options.c: State civil service legislation is breached because K. uses in her teaching the knowledge and experience gained while working at the Federal Service for Environmental Protection
options.d: There is a conflict of interest because, to obtain the material benefit of remuneration at her main place of work, K. uses knowledge and experience gained while working at the Federal Service for Environmental Protection

MT4-0592.stem: A civil servant's child turned 18 in February 2014. When submitting information on income, property and property-related obligations for 2013 in March 2014, the civil servant did not provide information about that child. In this situation:

options.a: The civil servant did not breach the law because the child had already reached adulthood when the information was submitted
options.b: The civil servant breached the law, but if a review shows that they acted in good faith overall and omitted the information because of a misunderstanding, the employer's representative may allow the missing information to be submitted, including without imposing liability for late submission
options.c: The civil servant breached the law, but if a review shows that they acted in good faith overall and omitted the information because of a misunderstanding, the employer's representative may allow the missing information to be submitted; a sanction for late submission must nevertheless be imposed
options.d: The civil servant must be held liable for submitting incomplete and/or inaccurate information
